outcome: No proof of the Nakai conjecture for all complex varieties has been found. Since 26 January 2024 it has been verified only for restricted classes of isolated hypersurface singularities (Xiao–Yau–Zhu–Zuo, Annali SNS, published 20 Dec 2024; Li–Xiao–Zuo, arXiv 7 Feb 2025; Yau–Zhu–Zuo, arXiv 27 Apr 2026), and a 6 Oct 2026 OpenAI catalogue entry claims a characteristic-zero counterexample to the closely related Lipman–Zariski conjecture, which I could not read at source and which has no public verification.
problem_asks: (1) Setting: a complex algebraic variety V, with its ring of differential operators D(V) (Grothendieck differential operators, the union of the order-n operators). (2) Hypothesis: D(V) is generated by the derivations (order-one operators) it contains. (3) Conclusion: V is smooth. The statement is one universal claim over all complex algebraic varieties, of any dimension and not restricted to affine ones. The commonly quoted equivalent form (Nakai; Singh 1986) is that for every n ≥ 2 the operators of order ≤ n are generated by those of order ≤ 1, which should force regularity. Context, not part of the ask: the conjecture implies the Zariski–Lipman conjecture (Becker; Rego, as stated in arXiv:2604.24508).

events.what_happened: Mount and Villamayor, 'On a conjecture of Y. Nakai', Osaka J. Math. 10 (1973) 325–327: proves the Nakai conjecture for affine coordinate rings of irreducible algebraic curves. Recorded from the Wikipedia article's reference list (opened); the paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: Nakai's conjecture for coordinate rings of irreducible algebraic curves (dimension one). Settles that class completely.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 1973 (per the Wikipedia reference list)

events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for curves; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Schreiner, 'On a conjecture of Nakai', Archiv der Mathematik 62 (1994) 506–512: proves the Nakai conjecture for Stanley–Reisner rings. Recorded from the Wikipedia article (opened); the paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: Nakai's conjecture for Stanley–Reisner rings (combinatorial, generally singular affine rings). Settles that class.
events.remains: Varieties outside the Stanley–Reisner class, including all singular varieties not covered by the other listed classes.

events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for this class; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Becker, 'Higher derivations and the Zariski–Lipman conjecture', Proc. Symp. Pure Math. 30 (1977), and Rego (year not confirmed): show that the Nakai conjecture implies the Zariski–Lipman conjecture. A 1977 J. Algebra paper, 'The Zariski–Lipman Conjecture' (J. Algebra 47 (1977) 411–424, authors not confirmed), is reported in a search summary to show that if the derivation module is free then higher derivations are free and generated by first-order ones, which would make Nakai's hypothesis hold for such rings. I did not open either 1977 paper; this is from the arXiv:2604.24508 introduction (opened) and a search-snippet summary of the J. Algebra paper.
events.delivers: A conditional implication: Nakai's conjecture ⇒ Zariski–Lipman conjecture. Per the search-snippet summary, freeness of the derivation module implies that higher derivations are generated by first-order ones (for the analytic local setting described there). It does not settle Nakai.
events.remains: Nakai's conjecture itself; the Zariski–Lipman conjecture in general.
events.doubts: The mechanism is known only from a search summary; the setting (analytic local rings versus finitely generated algebras over C) is not confirmed. This matters for whether a free-derivation counterexample to Zariski–Lipman would also violate Nakai's hypothesis (see openai-2026-lipman-zariski).
events.direction: Conditional implication that links Nakai to Zariski–Lipman; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Balwant Singh (1986) states a higher-order form of the Nakai conjecture (generation of order-≤n operators by order-≤1 operators, for each n ≥ 2) and reportedly proves it for plane curves and for cones in 3-space. Known only from a search-snippet summary of a later arXiv paper; the 1986 paper was not opened.
events.delivers: A bounded-order variant of Nakai's hypothesis; results for plane curves and cones in 3-space (per the summary). This is a different formulation of the question, not the question as stated.
events.remains: The original Nakai statement for those classes and for all other varieties.
events.doubts: Known only from a search snippet; not verified against the 1986 paper.
events.direction: Variant of the conjecture; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Brumatti, Lequain, Levcovitz, Simis, 'A note on the Nakai conjecture', Proc. AMS 130 (2002) 15–21: gives counterexamples to the Nakai and Zariski–Lipman conjectures in the class of one-dimensional pseudo-geometric local domains containing a field of characteristic zero. The AMS page returned 403; the description comes from search-result snippets and a summary of the abstract.
events.delivers: Counterexamples to the Nakai conjecture for one-dimensional pseudo-geometric local domains containing a characteristic-zero field, which are not finitely generated algebras over a field. This is an analogue of the variety question on a different class of rings, so it does not settle the variety statement.
events.remains: The conjecture for rings essentially of finite type over a characteristic-zero field, i.e. for varieties (the authors say these remain open).

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the note in 2002 (vol. 130, no. 1, pp. 15–21, per search metadata)

events.direction: Counterexample to the Nakai conjecture, but for a different class of rings (one-dimensional, pseudo-geometric, not finite type). It does not answer the variety question.
events.object: One-dimensional pseudo-geometric local domains containing a characteristic-zero field, for which the Nakai conjecture fails (construction not read). Not a complex variety.

events.what_happened: Xiao, Yau, Zuo, 'On higher order derivations associated to isolated hypersurface singularities', Asian J. Math. 29(4) (2025) 485–516 (per the Tsinghua publication list, dated 17 Sept 2026). The abstract, as summarised, verifies the Nakai conjecture for Brieskorn singularities and an inequality conjecture on dim Der²/Der¹ for binomial singularities. The PDF (Tsinghua PureMath/485.pdf) was not readable here, so this is from search summaries and the publication list. The first public version has not been located.
events.delivers: The Nakai conjecture for isolated Brieskorn hypersurface singularities (per the summary). One search summary of a later paper describes this as weighted homogeneous Brieskorn singularities, which is broader; the discrepancy is not resolved here.
events.remains: Non-Brieskorn isolated hypersurface singularities; all other varieties.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published as vol. 29, no. 4 (2025), pp. 485–516, per the authors' own publication list

events.remains: Non-homogeneous isolated hypersurface singularities and all other varieties.

The arXiv abstract page was opened; the main theorem was read from a summary of the HTML version.

events.what_happened: Stephen S.-T. Yau, Qiwei Zhu, Huaiqing Zuo, 'Nakai conjectures for isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularities', arXiv:2604.24508 [math.AG]. Versions: v1 27 Apr 2026; v2 18 Aug 2026; v3 19 Aug 2026; v4 8 Oct 2026 (current when opened). For A = k[x]/(f), k algebraically closed of characteristic zero, f weighted homogeneous with an isolated singularity at 0, the paper shows that a second-order derivation of A exists that is not generated by first-order derivations (also after localising), which by Singh's second-order criterion verifies the Nakai conjecture for that class. Its introduction (v4) says that 'Recently, OpenAI has claimed to find a counterexample' to the characteristic-zero Lipman–Zariski conjecture and that the claim 'has not yet been verified by the mathematical community'. These sentences were read through a WebFetch summary, not verbatim.
events.revisions: v1 27 Apr 2026; v2 18 Aug 2026; v3 19 Aug 2026; v4 8 Oct 2026 (version history from the arXiv abstract page). Which version first carried the OpenAI sentence is not established; v4 is after OpenAI's 6 Oct 2026 release.
events.delivers: Verifies the Nakai conjecture for isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularities (A = k[x]/(f), k algebraically closed of characteristic zero), via a second-order derivation not generated by first-order ones.
events.remains: Isolated hypersurface singularities that are not weighted homogeneous; non-hypersurface singularities; all other complex varieties.
events.direction: Verifies the conjecture for a class; no counterexample. Its introduction also reports the OpenAI Lipman–Zariski claim as unverified.
events.object: A second-order derivation of A = k[x]/(f) (f weighted homogeneous, isolated singularity) that is not generated by first-order derivations, found by solving linear systems over the quotient ring. It witnesses the strict inclusion Der²(A) ⊋ (second-order operators generated by Der¹), so it confirms rather than refutes the conjecture for that class. Explicit construction.

events.what_happened: On 6 Oct 2026 OpenAI published on GitHub (openai/math, commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a) a catalogue of 722 manuscripts in 372 families, which its README says are 'produced by an internal OpenAI model'. Family 048 is titled 'A characteristic-zero counterexample to Lipman–Zariski', with one manuscript at preprints/A-singular-normal-affine-surface-with-free-tangent-sheaf-September-23-2026/paper.pdf (the directory's README is dated 23 Sept 2026). Secondary descriptions (a University of Pittsburgh catalogue by Hajlasz, not opened, and the kingy.ai index of the release) say the claimed result is a singular, normal, affine complex surface whose tangent sheaf is free of rank two, which would disprove the Lipman–Zariski conjecture in characteristic zero. I could not open the manuscript (PDF not readable with the available tools), so the equation, the construction and any statement about the ring of differential operators are unknown.
events.revisions: Manuscript dated 23 Sept 2026 by its directory name; first public release 6 Oct 2026 (repository). On 7 Oct 2026 OpenAI withdrew three manuscripts (sign error; reported titles: 'Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds', 'Algebraicity of Kuga–Satake Correspondences for K3 Surfaces', 'The rational Hodge conjecture for products of K3 surfaces'), revised 14 others, and the catalogue now lists 719. Family 048 is not among the reported withdrawals; whether it was among the 14 revisions is not known.
events.delivers: As claimed by the catalogue (not read at source): a counterexample to the Lipman–Zariski conjecture in characteristic zero, namely a singular normal affine complex surface with free rank-two tangent sheaf. Lipman–Zariski is a different conjecture from Nakai. It bears on Nakai through the literature's statement that Nakai implies Lipman–Zariski (Becker; Rego): if the derivation module is free, the literature summary above suggests Nakai's generation hypothesis holds for that ring, in which case the surface would contradict Nakai. Whether this surface's ring of differential operators is generated by its derivations was not established from anything I could read.
events.remains: Nakai's conjecture is not addressed by this entry's title; it is unaffected unless the surface satisfies Nakai's hypothesis (ring of differential operators generated by derivations). The Lipman–Zariski conjecture is affected in the claimed case; the normal-surface case, which the literature treats as the main open case, is the one the claim would fall in.
events.doubts: (1) Catalogue-level claim from an internal, unreleased model; OpenAI's README says 'not all have accompanying Lean formalizations' and 'some of the unformalized results could have issues'. (2) The Lean file formalization.yaml at that commit contains no entry mentioning Lipman, Zariski or tangent sheaves, and the family page lean/docs/048.md returned 404; so no Lean formalisation of this entry was found. (3) An OpenAI spokesperson reportedly said roughly 50% of the results were released unconfirmed (Retraction Watch, opened). (4) Three other manuscripts in the same release were withdrawn for a sign error within a day. (5) The arXiv:2604.24508 v4 introduction says the claim 'has not yet been verified by the mathematical community'. (6) The manuscript has not been read, so I cannot say whether it is correct or whether it avoids the known classes (the literature says Lipman–Zariski is known for many normal-surface classes, e.g. log canonical, Graf; Bergner–Graf for complex surfaces with pg − g − b ≤ 2). I found no expert statement on this entry.
events.direction: Claims a counterexample to Lipman–Zariski, which would contradict Nakai for that surface if the surface also satisfies Nakai's hypothesis (derivations generating differential operators). Does not address Nakai directly as far as I could tell.
events.object: Per catalogue summaries only: a singular, normal, affine complex surface whose tangent sheaf is free of rank two, claimed to disprove Lipman–Zariski in characteristic zero. Its equation and whether the construction is explicit or existential are not known; the manuscript was not readable.

events.what_happened: The manuscript ('A singular normal affine surface with free tangent sheaf') says nothing about rings of differential operators, D(V), or Nakai's conjecture. A search of its build sources finds no mention of either. Its only claim in this area is the Lipman–Zariski counterexample in the entry above: a normal affine surface A with Der_C(A) ≅ A⊕A and A_m not regular.
events.delivers: No claim about the Nakai hypothesis or conclusion. The manuscript does not show that the ring of differential operators of A, or of any other variety, is generated by its order-one operators. The family bears on Nakai only through the implication that the problem's context cites, namely that Nakai's conjecture implies Zariski–Lipman (Becker; Rego). If that implication holds, refuting Zariski–Lipman as this family does would also refute Nakai's conjecture. The manuscript neither states nor uses that route, and it does not verify the Nakai hypothesis for A. So the family does not settle Nakai on its own argument.
events.remains: All of the Nakai problem as far as these manuscripts go: whether any singular complex variety, including the constructed A, has its ring of differential operators generated by derivations, and the order-n form for n ≥ 2 quoted in the problem context.
events.doubts: The manuscript does not discuss differential operators at all, so nothing in the text checks the Nakai hypothesis for any variety. Any reading that counts this family as refuting Nakai depends entirely on the external implication.; conditional on: Bearing on Nakai requires the implication Nakai ⇒ Zariski–Lipman, which the manuscript neither states nor proves. I did not check the cited source (arXiv:2604.24508) and did not search for it. It also requires that the ring of differential operators of the constructed A, or of a variety derived from it, is generated by derivations, which the text does not address.
events.direction: no direct direction; refutes Zariski–Lipman, which bears on Nakai only via the cited implication

summary: Found no proof of the Nakai conjecture for all complex varieties since 26 January 2024. The in-window events are verifications for restricted classes of singularities, and they come from one group (Yau, Zhu, Xiao, Zuo, with Li) whose papers cite one another. The Annali SNS paper (Xiao–Yau–Zhu–Zuo) was published 20 Dec 2024 and is cited by the 2025 and 2026 preprints; I did not find an earlier preprint, though the Tsinghua publication list (17 Sept 2026) still says 'to appear, 2026', which conflicts with the journal page. The 2024 Yau talk claims the homogeneous isolated hypersurface case, but I found no written argument for it, so I dated it to the talk. The arXiv preprints 2502.04672 (Feb 2025) and 2604.24508 (Apr 2026, v4 Oct 2026) are both on arXiv and are the only ones whose abstracts I could read directly. Nothing in any of these sources uses an AI system, and I found no AI or Lean work on Nakai itself (Lean search, Epoch's open-problem pilot list, the Erdős trackers, and Sra's counterexample survey all come up empty for it). The one in-window event that involves AI is OpenAI's 6 Oct 2026 release (openai/math, 722 manuscripts from an unreleased internal model). Its family 048 claims a characteristic-zero counterexample to the Lipman–Zariski conjecture: a singular normal affine complex surface with free rank-two tangent sheaf. Lipman–Zariski is a different conjecture, but the literature (Becker; Rego, as stated in arXiv:2604.24508 and in a search summary of a 1977 J. Algebra paper) says Nakai implies Lipman–Zariski. So, if the surface's ring of differential operators is generated by its derivations, the claim would also contradict Nakai. I could not open the manuscript (its PDF is not readable here), so the equation, the construction, and whether the Nakai hypothesis holds for this surface are all unverified. The claim also has no Lean formalisation at the repository snapshot I could read, and the Yau–Zhu–Zuo v4 introduction says it has not yet been verified by the community. The three withdrawn manuscripts in that release are on Hodge-type topics, not this one. Close calls: (a) whether the OpenAI entry is a Nakai event at all, depending on whether the surface satisfies Nakai's hypothesis; (b) whether the 2024 Yau talk counts, since it has no written argument; (c) whether the Xiao–Yau–Zhu–Zuo date should be the journal date or an earlier preprint date.
competing_reading: (a) The OpenAI entry is a Lipman–Zariski event and not a Nakai event: the title, the catalogue and the author's own README all concern Lipman–Zariski, and the Nakai hypothesis (differential operators generated by derivations) is never stated for this surface, so Nakai is untouched. (b) Against that, the literature says Nakai implies Lipman–Zariski, so a free-derivation singular surface is at least a candidate Nakai counterexample if the Becker–Rego lemma (free derivation module implies generation of higher derivations by first-order derivations) applies in the complex affine setting. That lemma was only seen in a search summary of a 1977 J. Algebra paper, and its hypotheses are not confirmed. The Yau–Zhu–Zuo v4 introduction, as summarised, reports the OpenAI claim as a counterexample to Lipman–Zariski and says it is unverified; I did not confirm whether it discusses Nakai's consequences for that surface. On the Annali date: the journal page says published 20 Dec 2024, while the authors' own list says 'to appear, 2026'; if the 2026 date is right the event moves into the window in a different way. On the 2024 Yau talk: the claim covers isolated homogeneous hypersurface singularities and may be subsumed by the 2026 weighted homogeneous result, which would make it a duplicate rather than a separate advance.
what_would_settle_it: (1) Read openai/math preprints/A-singular-normal-affine-surface-with-free-tangent-sheaf-September-23-2026/paper.pdf: the surface's equation, whether the tangent sheaf is free of rank two, whether it is normal and affine over C, and whether its ring of differential operators is generated by derivations. Together these decide whether the entry is a Nakai event. (2) The hypotheses of the Becker/Rego lemma (analytic local versus finitely generated over C), from Becker 1977 or the 1977 J. Algebra paper. (3) An arXiv version or referee report for the Annali paper, and a published version of the Yau–Zhu–Zuo homogeneous result. (4) A named expert's check of the OpenAI surface (for example the Lipman–Zariski specialists cited in the literature), or a Lean formalisation of family 048. (5) The Li–Xiao–Zuo and Yau–Zhu–Zuo texts themselves, to check the main theorems verbatim (I read them through summaries only).

event.what_happened: Stephen S.-T. Yau, talk 'Nakai Conjecture for Homogeneous Isolated Hypersurface Singularity', BIMSA AG Seminar, Thursday 20 June 2024. The abstract states 'we prove the Nakai Conjecture for isolated homogeneous hypersurface singularities'. No written argument for this claim was located. Li–Xiao–Zuo (2025) cites a 'Yau–Zhu–Zuo' result for isolated homogeneous hypersurface singularities as recent; no preprint or journal record was found under that author list.

judgement.why: Every post-snapshot Nakai result proves the conjecture for a restricted class of isolated hypersurface singularities (Brieskorn, fewnomial/cusp, modality ≤ 2, homogeneous, weighted homogeneous), so each is a case that confirms it. The two journal papers are digested by journal acceptance. The preprints are unreviewed, and so is the talk, which has no written argument and is doubtful. The OpenAI family 048 entries claim a counterexample to Lipman–Zariski, a different conjecture. The manuscript, which the second entry read, never addresses rings of differential operators or Nakai's hypothesis. Nakai ⇒ Lipman–Zariski would make a Lipman–Zariski counterexample a Nakai counterexample by contraposition, but that implication is known only from secondary summaries whose setting is unconfirmed. So I score those entries as variant: the model generated them, and they settle no part of the Nakai question on the record. Brumatti et al. is a variant because it concerns non-finite-type rings, and Singh's bounded-order reformulation is a variant too. The Yau–Zhu–Zuo derivation is an internal tool, not an object the statement asks for, so its object_role is null.
judgement.doubts: The two OpenAI entries describe one release of one manuscript and are duplicates. If Nakai ⇒ Lipman–Zariski holds unconditionally for complex affine varieties (Becker; Rego), a correct family 048 surface would refute Nakai outright, and the scope would become whole/refuted (unreviewed). The record could not confirm the hypotheses of that implication. The Annali date conflicts with the authors' list ('to appear, 2026'), but both dates fall after the snapshot. The Xiao–Yau–Zuo event has only a year (2025), which still falls after the snapshot.
